title: Personality Assessment: Projective & Objective
summary: Personality assessment methods: projective tests (Rorschach inkblot, TAT) and objective inventories (MMPI, 16PF), with their principles, uses and limitations.
objectives: Describe projective tests and their rationale.
revision: Personality assessment: projective tests (Rorschach, TAT) using ambiguous stimuli vs objective inventories (MMPI, 16PF) with standardised scoring.
traps: Projective = ambiguous stimuli, clinical interpretation (Rorschach, TAT).

notes.t: Assessment using ambiguous stimuli; the person projects unconscious thoughts, feelings and conflicts onto the stimulus.
Respondents describe what they see in symmetrical inkblots; responses are scored for content, location and determinants.
Respondents tell stories about ambiguous pictures, revealing needs, motives and conflicts.
Standardised questionnaire with fixed questions and scored responses (e.g., MMPI, 16PF).
Minnesota Multiphasic Personality Inventory — clinical assessment of psychopathology using true/false items.
Cattell's Sixteen Personality Factor Questionnaire measuring 16 source traits.
UGC NET frequently contrasts projective techniques with objective inventories and asks about Rorschach, TAT, MMPI and 16PF.

mnemonics.title: RTOM
mnemonics.text: R — Rorschach (projective), T — TAT (projective), O — objective inventory, M — MMPI/16PF (objective)

flashcards.a: Ambiguous stimuli; person projects unconscious content.
Inkblot test; responses scored for content, location, determinants.
